propositions.text: Fengling Xu, Min Jin Yang, and their son sought protection in Canada under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
Ms. Xu fears persecution in China as a Falun Gong practitioner and due to family planning practices.
Mr. Yang is a citizen of China and Guyana, fears persecution in Guyana due to ethnicity, and claims protection.
Ms. Xu and son make similar claims regarding Guyana; Mr. Yang also claims protection in China as spouse of Falun Gong practitioner.
All three relied on Ms. Xu's personal narrative to support their protection claims.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Xu family members sought protection in Canada under IRPA, fearing persecution in China and Guyana, relying on Xu's narrative.

propositions.text: The Refugee Protection Division (RPD) heard the claims jointly on May 4, 2017, and rejected them on May 24, 2017.
RPD member found applicants' identities and nationalities established.
RPD found discrimination against Chinese in Guyana but not persecution or need for protection for Mr. Yang; risk was generalized violence.
RPD found Ms. Xu and son had access to Guyanese nationals' rights, thus excluded under Article 1E of Refugee Convention.
RPD did not exempt Ms. Xu and son from Article 1E as findings on Mr. Yang applied equally; did not address China claims.

paragraphs.summary: The court reports the RPD rejected claims, found identities established, discrimination but no persecution in Guyana, and excluded Xu and son under Article 1E.

propositions.text: Applicants appealed to Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) without new evidence or hearing request.
RAD confirmed RPD decision and dismissed appeal on January 29, 2018.

paragraphs.summary: The court states applicants appealed to RAD, which confirmed RPD's decision and dismissed the appeal.

propositions.text: Applicants allege RAD denied procedural fairness by deciding state protection issue without notice or opportunity to address it.
Applicants argue RAD's findings on lack of nexus to Convention ground, nature of risk in Guyana, and Article 1E exclusion are unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RAD denied procedural fairness and made unreasonable findings on nexus, risk, and Article 1E exclusion.

propositions.text: Court allows judicial review application.
Court finds RAD's Article 1E exclusion determination unreasonable.
Court finds RAD breached procedural fairness in considering state protection issue.
Court orders a new hearing as a result.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows judicial review, finds RAD's Article 1E ruling unreasonable and procedural fairness breached, requiring a new hearing.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu born in China July 1977; Mr. Yang born China November 1975; son born China August 2003; all Chinese nationals by birth.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the birth dates and Chinese nationality of Ms. Xu, Mr. Yang, and their son.

propositions.text: Mr. Yang left China in February 2004 to work in Guyana and support family.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Mr. Yang left China in 2004 to work in Guyana.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu faced medical problems in China due to family planning policies and joined husband in Guyana in December 2010; son stayed with grandparents in China.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Ms. Xu joined husband in Guyana in 2010 due to medical problems; son remained in China.

propositions.text: Mr. Yang gained Guyanese citizenship in May 2013 and bought a restaurant; both worked there.
Ms. Xu's narrative reports two armed robberies at the restaurant in December 2013 and May 2014; Ms. Xu assaulted during first robbery.
After second robbery, couple decided to sell restaurant and leave Guyana; Ms. Xu left June 16, 2014; Mr. Yang stayed to sell restaurant.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Mr. Yang became Guyanese citizen, bought restaurant, faced robberies, and couple decided to leave Guyana.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu's difficulties with family planning continued in China; she took up Falun Gong on cousin's advice.
On August 31, 2014, a Falun Gong session Ms. Xu attended was raided by Public Security Bureau; she escaped and hid.
Ms. Xu arranged to leave China with son for US; met Mr. Yang in Seattle February 2015; all entered Canada irregularly near Vancouver.
They submitted refugee claims in Toronto about one month after entering Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Ms. Xu faced persecution in China, fled with son to US, then entered Canada irregularly and claimed refugee protection.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu and Mr. Yang submitted Basis of Claim Forms relying on Ms. Xu's narrative.
Each applicant raised distinct claims regarding China and Guyana.
Ms. Xu's narrative summarized fears: arrest in China for Falun Gong, forced IUD, son's safety, husband's fear in Guyana and China due to ethnicity and Falun Gong.

paragraphs.summary: The court states applicants relied on Ms. Xu's narrative outlining fears of persecution in China and Guyana.

propositions.text: Applicants' counsel filed written submissions after RPD hearing relying on Ms. Xu's narrative.
Legal submissions focused on identity, credibility, and exclusion regarding Guyanese status.
RPD member's reasons show no different view of material issues in case.

paragraphs.summary: The court states counsel's submissions focused on identity, credibility, and exclusion; RPD agreed on material issues.

propositions.text: RPD member satisfied identity established but rejected claims under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
RPD limited analysis to claims regarding Guyana.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RPD found identity established but rejected claims, focusing on Guyana.

propositions.text: RPD accepted restaurant robberies occurred but found no future risk engaging sections 96 or 97.
Even if robberies were due to ethnicity, risk related to restaurant now sold; no evidence claimants couldn't live safely in other jobs.
Some discrimination against ethnic Chinese in Guyana but not persecution; risk was general crime risk.
RPD made no findings on state protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RPD found robberies not future risk, discrimination not persecution, and no state protection findings.

propositions.text: RPD found Federal Court of Appeal decision in Tretsetsang determinative regarding Ms. Xu and son.
RPD found Ms. Xu and son had access to Guyanese nationals' rights and excluded under Article 1E due to no reasonable efforts to obtain citizenship.
RPD found sections 96 and 97 not engaged for Ms. Xu and son regarding Guyana.
RPD found no evidence Falun Gong practitioners persecuted in Guyana or Ms. Xu forced to wear IUD there; claim not advanced on this basis.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RPD excluded Ms. Xu and son under Article 1E, found no persecution in Guyana, and no IRPA protection engaged.

propositions.text: Applicants identified three appeal issues: RPD errors on nexus to Convention ground, generalized risk in Guyana, and Article 1E exclusion for Ms. Xu and son.

paragraphs.summary: Applicants argue RPD erred on nexus, risk, and Article 1E exclusion issues in their appeal submissions.

propositions.text: Minister did not participate in the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Minister did not participate in the appeal.

propositions.text: RAD member applied Federal Court of Appeal decision in Huruglica and RAD panel decision in X (Re) for standard of review.
RAD reviews RPD decisions applying correctness standard for fact and mixed fact-law findings.
RAD may apply reasonableness standard if RPD has meaningful advantage, modified for RAD context.
None of appeal grounds were decided on reasonableness standard; credibility was not an issue.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD applied correctness standard per Huruglica and X (Re), with no reasonableness standard used and no credibility issue.

propositions.text: RAD dismissed the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD dismissed the appeal.

propositions.text: RAD found RPD's statement on robberies and ethnicity less clear but rejected applicants' claim of ethnic risk in Guyana.
RAD reviewed documentary evidence and concluded applicants failed to establish well-founded fear of targeting on Convention ground.
RAD agreed with RPD that applicants failed to establish nexus between fears and Convention ground.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD found RPD's reasoning unclear but agreed applicants failed to prove ethnic risk or nexus to Convention ground.

propositions.text: Whether applicants personally face a risk not generally faced by others in Guyana under IRPA s 97(1)(b)(ii)
Applicants' fear of crime is a risk generally faced by others in Guyana
Applicants have not rebutted presumption that state protection is unavailable in Guyana
Evidence does not support applicants' claim of being specifically targeted due to Chinese ethnicity
Protection is not available to applicants

paragraphs.summary: The RAD member found applicants' fear of crime is general in Guyana, they failed to rebut lack of state protection, and were not specifically targeted due to ethnicity, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Mr. Yang is excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E of the Refugee Convention
Ms. Xu and her son have access to rights of Guyanese nationals under Article 1E and are excluded from refugee consideration

paragraphs.summary: The RAD member agreed with the RPD that Mr. Yang is excluded under Article 1E and that Ms. Xu and her son have rights in Guyana excluding them from refugee consideration.

propositions.text: RAD confirmed RPD decision under IRPA s 111(1)(a) and dismissed appeal

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirmed the RPD decision and dismissed the appeal, per earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: RAD's factual and mixed fact-law determinations reviewed on reasonableness standard (Huruglica para 35)
Reasonableness review concerns substantive outcome and articulation process (Igloo Vikski para 18)
Reviewing court must consider outcome and reasons (Delta Air Lines para 27)
Decision must show justification, transparency, intelligibility and be within acceptable outcomes (Dunsmuir para 47)
Reasons must allow court to understand decision and assess acceptability (Newfoundland Nurses para 16)
Court intervenes only if criteria unmet; no reweighing evidence or substituting views (Khosa paras 59,61)

paragraphs.summary: The court explains the reasonableness standard for reviewing RAD decisions, citing multiple authorities on criteria and limits of review.

propositions.text: No standard of review for procedural fairness breaches; court decides fairness itself (Khosa para 43; CPR v Canada para 54)

paragraphs.summary: For procedural fairness issues, the court determines fairness itself without applying a standard of review, per prior authorities.

propositions.text: Is RAD's exclusion of applicants under Article 1E unreasonable?
Did RAD deny procedural fairness by deciding state protection issue without notice or opportunity to respond?
Is RAD's conclusion that applicants failed to establish well-founded fear of persecution unreasonable?
Is RAD's conclusion that applicants failed to establish need for protection unreasonable?

paragraphs.summary: The court frames four issues: Article 1E exclusion reasonableness, procedural fairness denial, and two reasonableness issues on fear of persecution and need for protection.

propositions.text: Applicants did not present grounds in this order but first two issues are determinative
No need to address other two issues

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the first two issues determinative and declines to address the other two, explaining applicants' order differed.

propositions.text: Brief review of RAD's role may be helpful before judicial review grounds

paragraphs.summary: The court introduces a brief review of the RAD's role before analyzing judicial review grounds.

propositions.text: IRPA s 110(1) allows appeal to RAD on law, fact, or mixed questions from RPD decisions
IRPA s 110(2) limits appeals in certain cases but no other ground limitations where appeal exists

paragraphs.summary: The court explains IRPA provisions allowing appeals to RAD on various grounds and some limitations.

propositions.text: IRPA s 110(3) requires RAD appeals to proceed without hearing on RPD record
IRPA ss 110(4)-(6) allow exceptions for new evidence and hearings if conditions met
FCA in Singh explained restrictions on new evidence preserve process integrity and finality (paras 43,50)

paragraphs.summary: The court describes IRPA rules on RAD appeals proceeding without hearing, exceptions for new evidence, and FCA's reasoning on finality.

propositions.text: RAD appeal is not a true de novo proceeding (Huruglica para 79)
RAD reviews RPD decision and conducts own analysis to determine RPD error (Huruglica para 103)

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD appeals are not de novo but involve reviewing RPD decisions and conducting own analysis per Huruglica.

propositions.text: RAD can correct errors of fact, law, or mixed fact-law made by RPD (Huruglica paras 78,103)
RAD reviews RPD findings on correctness standard but may defer on credibility if RPD has advantage (Huruglica para 70)
RAD may confirm, set aside and substitute, or refer back RPD decisions (IRPA s 111(1),(2))

paragraphs.summary: The court explains RAD's broad mandate to correct RPD errors, standards of review, and possible outcomes under IRPA.

propositions.text: RAD can confirm RPD decision on another basis but must respect natural justice and fairness
RAD must give notice and opportunity to parties before confirming on new basis not framed by parties (citing cases)
If RAD makes new substantive findings, it must give notice and opportunity to respond (Husian para 10)

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD must give notice and opportunity before confirming RPD decisions on new bases, citing authorities and Husian.

propositions.text: Article 1E excludes persons recognized by competent authorities as having rights and obligations of nationality in that country

paragraphs.summary: The court states Article 1E of the Refugee Convention excludes persons recognized as having nationality rights in the country of residence.

propositions.text: RAD member's conclusions on Article 1E are puzzling in two respects

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RAD member's conclusions on Article 1E puzzling in two respects.

propositions.text: RAD member finds Mr. Yang excluded under Article 1E, apparently agreeing with RPD
RPD did not conclude Mr. Yang excluded under Article 1E
Ground of appeal on Article 1E concerns only Ms. Xu and her son
Mr. Yang sought protection regarding China and Guyana; burden on him to show fear of persecution in both under IRPA s 96(a)
Mr. Yang's situation unrelated to Article 1E exclusion

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RAD's exclusion of Mr. Yang under Article 1E is unsupported, unrelated to appeal grounds, and irrelevant to his burden under IRPA.

propositions.text: RAD member states Ms. Xu and son have rights in Guyana under Article 1E and are excluded
RPD found Ms. Xu and son excluded under Article 1E on erroneous basis relying on Tretsetsang
Tretsetsang concerns IRPA s 96(a), not Article 1E
RAD member does not mention RPD's flawed analysis but conducts own analysis under Zeng
RAD's analysis under Zeng is unreasonable

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD's Article 1E exclusion of Ms. Xu and son was erroneous, RAD did not note this but did own analysis which is unreasonable.

propositions.text: Zeng test for Article 1E exclusion: claimant status similar to nationals in third country excludes claimant; if lost status, consider factors including reason, return risk, obligations, other facts

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Zeng test for Article 1E exclusion involving claimant's status and balancing factors.

propositions.text: RAD member answered Zeng test questions as follows

paragraphs.summary: The court introduces how the RAD member answered the Zeng test questions.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu and son did not have status substantially similar to nationals in Guyana at hearing time
They were not excluded from refugee protection on this basis

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Ms. Xu and son lacked status similar to nationals in Guyana and thus were not excluded on that basis, per RAD member.

propositions.text: RAD member could not conclude Ms. Xu and son had status but Ms. Xu had right to reside in Guyana during that time

paragraphs.summary: The RAD member could not conclude Ms. Xu and her son had status but Ms. Xu had right to reside in Guyana during that time, says the court.

propositions.text: Ms. Xu and son had access to status similar to nationals of Guyana between Dec 2010 and June 2014
RAD member found Ms. Xu aware of ability to apply for status but took no action to normalize status
RAD member found Ms. Xu failed without good reason to preserve right to return to Guyana
RAD member concluded Ms. Xu and son excluded from refugee protection under Article 1E of Refugee Convention

paragraphs.summary: The RAD member found Ms. Xu and son had access to status but took no action to normalize it and excluded them from refugee protection under Article 1E, says the court.

propositions.text: Applicants challenged RPD finding that Guyanese citizenship was within Ms. Xu and son's control
Canadian case law holds potential Guyanese citizenship not within spouse's control as it is discretionary
Evidence before RAD suggested discretion still applied but member did not address applicants' argument

paragraphs.summary: Applicants challenged RPD's control test; case law says citizenship is discretionary; RAD did not address this argument, says the court.

propositions.text: Whether case law on section 96(a) IRPA fits Zeng test is not determined
Determinative issue is RAD member's failure to consider Ms. Xu's explanation for not securing status in Guyana
Ms. Xu left Guyana after two violent armed robberies and feared further victimization
RPD and RAD did not disbelieve Ms. Xu's account of events
Even if events insufficient for sections 96 or 97 claims, they justify not normalizing status
Under Zeng, Ms. Xu's explanation for losing status must be considered
RAD member did not consider Ms. Xu's explanation, so exclusion under Article 1E lacks justification

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RAD failed to consider Ms. Xu's explanation for not securing status, making exclusion under Article 1E unjustified.

propositions.text: Applicants challenged RPD's findings on lack of nexus to Convention ground and lack of personalized risk
RAD upheld RPD's determinations but relied on evidence about Guyana authorities' protection efforts
Applicants say procedural fairness breached as they had no notice or chance to address state protection issue
Court agrees with applicants that procedural fairness was breached

paragraphs.summary: Applicants challenged RPD findings; RAD relied on state protection evidence without notice; court agrees procedural fairness breached.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness requires notice and opportunity to address new issues before RAD confirms RPD decision on new basis
No disagreement in jurisprudence about this principle or test for newness
Disputes arise only in applying principle in specific cases

paragraphs.summary: Court states procedural fairness requires notice and opportunity on new issues; principle undisputed; disputes arise in application.

propositions.text: Issue of state protection is new in this case and did not stem from issues framed by parties
Claimants must approach home state for protection before other states' responsibility engaged (Ward)
Home state's inability to protect is crucial to well-founded fear (Ward)
State protection not identified as material issue before RPD; no submissions or determinations on it
Applicants' appeal to RAD focused on lack of nexus; state protection issue not reasonably stemming from appeal issues
Applicants entitled to notice and opportunity to address state protection issue before RAD decision

paragraphs.summary: Court finds state protection issue new, not raised before RPD, not stemming from appeal issues; applicants entitled to notice and opportunity.

propositions.text: Respondent says state protection issue immaterial as RAD could uphold RPD decision without it
Some RAD reasons unrelated to state protection and free of reviewable error
Adverse outcome was legally inevitable despite procedural fairness breach

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues state protection issue immaterial; RAD could uphold decision without it; outcome legally inevitable despite breach.

propositions.text: Court not persuaded breach of procedural fairness should be overlooked due to legal inevitability

paragraphs.summary: Court is not persuaded to overlook procedural fairness breach due to legal inevitability.

propositions.text: Breach relates to claims vis-à-vis Guyana but applicants also made claims vis-à-vis China not examined on merits
Claims vis-à-vis China not examined due to erroneous exclusion under Article 1E
Court cannot say claims are doomed after proper consideration

paragraphs.summary: Court notes breach relates to Guyana claims; China claims unexamined due to exclusion; cannot say claims doomed after proper review.

propositions.text: State protection issue cannot be disentangled from RAD member's reasons, especially under section 97 IRPA
RAD member relied on finding applicants did not rebut presumption of state protection without submissions
Respondent says generalized risk finding alone is fatal to section 97 claims
Upholding result on respondent's basis would require rewriting member's reasons, exceeding judicial review bounds

paragraphs.summary: Court finds state protection issue integral to RAD reasons; respondent's alternative basis inadequate; rewriting reasons exceeds review scope.

propositions.text: State protection important under section 96 IRPA relating to nexus with Convention ground
RAD member diminished probative value of applicants' evidence due to context of state protection efforts
RPD member did not rely on state protection information
Applicants had no reason to address state protection significance until RAD reasons received, too late then

paragraphs.summary: Court finds state protection important to nexus issue; RAD diminished evidence due to it; applicants had no chance to address it before decision.

propositions.text: Failure to give notice and opportunity on state protection issue resulted in procedural fairness breach

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes failure to give notice and opportunity on state protection issue breached procedural fairness.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review allowed; RAD decision set aside; matter remitted for redetermination by different decision-maker

paragraphs.summary: Court allows judicial review, sets aside RAD decision, and remits matter for redetermination by different decision-maker.

propositions.text: Parties did not suggest serious questions of general importance for certification under section 74(d) IRPA
Court agrees no questions of general importance arise

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no serious questions of general importance for certification under section 74(d) IRPA.
